---
title: "MFA Success Rate"
description: "Share of second-factor attempts at sign-in that succeeded."
---

The proportion of [second-factor attempts](second-factor-attempts.qmd) at sign-in
that succeeded over a selected reporting period.

This metric is useful for monitoring how often users clear the second factor
when they sign in. A falling rate can point to user friction with a particular
factor, SMS delivery problems, or attack traffic.

It covers the factors the public can sign in with: `sms_otp`, `voice_otp`, and
`fido2` (passkeys). `email_otp` is not a second factor: it checks an email
address at sign-up, and its rate is [Sign-up Email Verification
Rate](sign-up-email-verification-rate.qmd). `kq`, `totp`, `qr`, and
`ibm_verify_push` are internal factors. For one rate per factor, including those,
see [MFA Success Rate by Factor](mfa-success-rate-by-factor.qmd).

## Calculation

Restrict to the sign-in factors. Divide the sum of `count` where
`result = 'success'` by the sum of `count` where `result` is `'success'` or
`'failure'`. OTP factor types also produce a `'sent'` event per challenge, which
must be excluded from both the numerator and the denominator, because `sent` rows
do not represent outcomes.

To track the metric over time, bin the same calculation by week. Truncating
`from_date` to the week groups each day into its Monday-anchored bin, so the
result is one success rate per Monday-to-Sunday week.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

Overall:

```sql
SELECT
    CAST(SUM(count) FILTER (WHERE result = 'success') AS DOUBLE)
        / NULLIF(SUM(count), 0) AS mfa_success_rate
FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_mfa_activity
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE CAST(from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
  -- the factors the public can sign in with; email_otp is a sign-up check
  AND mfa_type IN ('sms_otp', 'voice_otp', 'fido2')
  -- exclude "sent" rows; success rate is calculated from outcome events only.
  -- including "sent" would inflate the denominator and deflate the rate.
  AND result IN ('success', 'failure');
```

By week:

```sql
SELECT
    date_trunc('week', CAST(from_date AS DATE)) AS week_start,
    CAST(SUM(count) FILTER (WHERE result = 'success') AS DOUBLE)
        / NULLIF(SUM(count), 0) AS mfa_success_rate
FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_mfa_activity
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE CAST(from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
  -- the factors the public can sign in with; email_otp is a sign-up check
  AND mfa_type IN ('sms_otp', 'voice_otp', 'fido2')
  -- exclude "sent" rows; success rate is calculated from outcome events only.
  -- including "sent" would inflate the denominator and deflate the rate.
  AND result IN ('success', 'failure')
-- date_trunc('week', ...) anchors each bin to its Monday
GROUP BY date_trunc('week', CAST(from_date AS DATE))
ORDER BY week_start;
```

## R

Overall:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_mfa_activity")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-05-28"),
    # the factors the public can sign in with; email_otp is a sign-up check
    mfa_type %in% c("sms_otp", "voice_otp", "fido2"),
    # exclude "sent" rows; success rate is calculated from outcome events only.
    # including "sent" would inflate the denominator and deflate the rate.
    result %in% c("success", "failure")
  ) |>
  summarise(
    mfa_success_rate =
      sum(if_else(result == "success", as.double(count), 0), na.rm = TRUE) /
        sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

By week:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_mfa_activity")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-05-28"),
    # the factors the public can sign in with; email_otp is a sign-up check
    mfa_type %in% c("sms_otp", "voice_otp", "fido2"),
    # exclude "sent" rows; success rate is calculated from outcome events only.
    # including "sent" would inflate the denominator and deflate the rate.
    result %in% c("success", "failure")
  ) |>
  # floor_date(..., "week") translates to Athena's date_trunc('week', ...),
  # which anchors each bin to its Monday
  mutate(week_start = floor_date(as.Date(from_date), "week")) |>
  group_by(week_start) |>
  summarise(
    mfa_success_rate =
      sum(if_else(result == "success", as.double(count), 0), na.rm = TRUE) /
        sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(week_start)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

The rate is a proportion between 0 and 1. Interpret per factor
where possible: a low overall rate may be driven by a single struggling factor
rather than a system-wide problem. In the weekly view, the first and last weeks
of the reporting window are usually partial (the window rarely starts or ends on
a Monday), so treat boundary weeks with caution when comparing trends.

## Alternative names

- MFA pass rate
- second-factor success rate
- sign-in MFA success rate
- MFA completion rate
